title: List of games that use LLMs for gameplay?
author: technaturalism
selftext: I only know of a few like AI Rogue Lite and Rogue Lite 2d. Any other notable examples of games that actually use AI for gameplay elements?

comments.author: Original_Bell580
comments.body:
They are primarily research tools, however I designed them like games. Largely unknown for now.  
\- \[LlmSandbox\]([https://github.com/Trainerx7979/LlmSandbox](https://github.com/Trainerx7979/LlmSandbox)) - Real-time 2D NPC sandbox where procedurally generated agents live, move, and make decisions via local LLM (Ollama/LM Studio). Features memory, relationships, goal-setting, and a developer console for injecting commands.

\- \[LLM-Sim-Alpha\]([https://github.com/Trainerx7979/LLM-Sim-Alpha](https://github.com/Trainerx7979/LLM-Sim-Alpha)) - Research-oriented emergent-behavior simulation where one NPC is secretly evil. Full JSONL logging of every agent brain state, visual log replay viewer, and configurable storyteller alignments. Built for studying emergent social dynamics.

Both are free and open-source, available on the github links. They use LOCAL Ollama or LM Studio endpoints, and are easily re-configurable to fit multiple similar scenarios. LlmSandbox is even capable of carrying out intent by translating your instruction in real-time into actions and messages sent to specific NPCs in order to attain the effect you directed.

They are fun, they are entertaining, and if you want to research behavior in LLMs, they have logs that are detailed. LLM-Agent-Alpha even has a visual log player included that gives you access to all prompts/responses and the state of the agent at each turn.  
Enjoy.

comments.author: FakeCarbonara
comments.body:
Made a game called 09:59 TO HEAVEN [09:59 TO HEAVEN](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4302630/9_MINUTES_AND_59_SECONDS_TO_HEAVEN/), you’ve got 10 minutes to convince God you deserve heaven. Full LLM conversation, no scripts.

The twist: God makes up the rules as He goes. No pre-written scoring, He decides your +1 or -1 on His own and tells you why. Unpredictable but fair. I think it’s the first game where even the scoring is generative.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

comments.author: Ser-Ramic
comments.body:
Runebook. https://runebook.gg. This is my AI story game that I built. It's a sandbox narrative engine where the player can type or say any move, and the LLM Storyteller generates the next passage while the game carries forward people, places, inventory, promises, and consequences.

For fantasy stories, the Storyteller can act as an AI Dungeon Master, but the same engine also supports mystery, horror, romance, historical drama, manga, and other genres.

The main design problem has been making those open-ended turns accumulate into a coherent story with an earned ending instead of an endless chat transcript.

It works in the browser for solo, co-op, or larger multiplayer stories and is currently in paid Early Access, with a free story start.
